\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis is an online E log book to discuss our patient's de-identified health data shared after taking his\/her\/guardian's signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patient's problems through series of inputs from global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs. This E log book also reflects my patient-centred online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\"I've been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of \"patient clinical data analysis\" to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings, investigations and come up with a diagnosis and treatment plan\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: red; font-size: large;\"\u003ECHIEF COMPLAINS\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E60 year old female daily wage labourer by occupation, resident of Tirumalagiri, mothkur \u0026nbsp;presented to the casualty on dec 25 th 2023 with the complains of pedal edema since 5 days, shortness of breath since 3 days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: red; font-size: large;\"\u003EBACKGROUND HISTORY\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBorn in a rural village, parents were daily wage labourers,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6 th member of the family, among 7 siblings, 3 brothers and 4 sisters\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; |\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUneducated, helped their parents in household things and at farm\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMarried at the age 14 yrs to a daily wage labourer\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHad 3 children - 2 sons and 1 daughter by the age of 20 yr\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGot all the children married and leading an uneventful life till 15 yrs ago \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #2b00fe;\"\u003EDaily routine :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u0026nbsp;wake-up at 4:30 am in the morning the couple together goes to farm for milking the cows and feed them\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGet back to home at 7 am in the morning\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECook their breakfast ( jowar roti, ragi Jawa , chapattis, Upma )\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGoes to their daily wage work from 9 am and come back to home by 6 pm, their work consisted of harvesting \u0026nbsp;rice fields , groundnut fields , cotton fields\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGets their dinner by 8 pm and goes to bed by 8:30 pm\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; |\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E15 yrs ago suddenly her elder son while driving tractor had accident and expired\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe couple was distressed a little as they had to look after their sons kids\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; |\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELater his elder son wife left the home and stayed with their parents\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; |\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E12 yrs ago patient had fever, burning micturition \u0026nbsp;with generalised weaknesss and was diagnosed as diagnosed as type II Diabetes mellitus and was taking Glimiperide 1 mg+ Metformin 500mg tablet once daily\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELater due to their old age they could not go to their daily wage works and started staying at home\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThey started depending on their younger son for their food\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETheir younger son was not taking care of them properly\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThey used to spend half of their month with son and half month with daughter\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHer husband had CVA \u0026nbsp;3 yrs ago on waking up from sleep and had right hemiparesis after \u0026nbsp;which he recovered gradually after 6 months\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient had family stressors in the form of property disputes between both the daughter in laws, they were not looked after and they did not have food and money for medications\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAbout 50 days ago Patient had vomitings daily 4 to 5 times watery in consistency, non projectile, non bilious, non blood stained, this continued for 4 to 5 days, and generalised weakness for which her daughter took her to local RMP and he gave iv fluids.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThen he noticed some swelling in the in the left foot up to \u0026nbsp;and small ulcer on the base of the 3 rd toe on plantar aspect\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe advised them to go for to a general surgeon for that wound management\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient \u0026nbsp;also developed blackish discolouration of the 3rd toe of left foot, the patient observed it 2 to 3 days after the symptoms started. \u0026nbsp;Patient was then taken to a general surgeon where they diagnosed her to have diabetic ulcer with gangrene and adviced amputation of the 3 rd toe and ulcer debridement\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDue to financial issues patient could not get it done there, and came to our hospital for further management\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;|\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient got admitted in our hospital on 13-12-2023 for diabetic wound management in general surgery department\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\n \u003Cimg border=\"0\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/a\/AVvXsEg3hxw5EVSutX1Cols68LgmE2BnIifClM_2f7LzFhhW0p6iM7wYFoHvPo6_En-AHHxCL-B_P4T4YianCH6b4MnqRa02E8BjUEhmn1OLBmjai-nSPDBNlihGz-P5qclxK4tfqJRvWi7Kca5-TRWYR6pJ8cAM96eBltyD2ZdVZToNmsED1gd8h9b94QSsBmM\" width=\"400\" \/\u003E\n \u003C\/a\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDuring the hospital stay patient was found to have decreased breath sounds, b\/l basal crepts and Pulmonology opinion was taken and diagnosed to have left upper lobe fungal ball and b\/l pleural effusions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBronchoscope was adviced for further evaluation and management but patient attenders were \u0026nbsp;not willing and \u0026nbsp;did not give consent for the procedure\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn 21 st December after the wound was found \u0026nbsp;to be in healing stage patient was discharged from the hospital\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; |\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was doing well in the home for 2 days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELater she gradually started developing shortness of breath\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: red; font-family: georgia; font-size: large;\"\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;66 yr old female presented with complains of pedal edema for both legs since 5 days and shortness of breath since 3 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPedal edema was \u0026nbsp;insidious in onset , pitting type extending up to the knee joint , not associated with pain.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShortness of breath since 3 days insidious in onset and gradually progressive, progressed from grade II to grade IV , associated with Orthopnea, no PND, no aggravating and relieving factors, no diurnal variations.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDecreased urine output since 3 days \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUlcer over the left foot on both plantar and dorsal aspect extending from the base of 3rd metatarsal to dorsum of the left foot\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo H\/o chest pain, palpitations, pedal edema, vomitings giddiness, loose stools, Excessive sweating.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: red; font-family: verdana; font-size: large;\"\u003EPAST HISTORY\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of diabetes since 12 years using human actrapid insulin since 1 week (previously \u0026nbsp;metformin 500mg and glimiperide Per oral once in the morning)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot a known case of hypertension, epilepsy, CAD, CVA, thyroid disorders, epilepsy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EH\/o disarticulation and debridement of 3rd toe of left foot 12 days back\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: red; font-size: large;\"\u003EFAMILY HISTORY\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo significant family history\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: red; font-family: times; font-size: large;\"\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAppetite decreased\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBowel and bladder movements normal\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMixed diet\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDrinks toddy occasionally once a month\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: red; font-size: large;\"\u003EGENERAL EXAMINATION\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient is drowsy , but arousable\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGCS- E 3 V 2 M5\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EModerately built and nourished\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPallor present\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPedal edema pitting type extending up to the knee joint\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo icterus, lymphadenopathy, clubbing, cyanosis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; Patient was intubated with 6.5 mm ET tube and the position was confirmed.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was connected to mechanical ventilator ACMV -VC mode , fio2-70%, PEEP- 5 mmhg, RR- 16 \/min , VT- 450ml and started on sedatives and paralytics.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient had paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia patient was given adenosine dose and later started on amiodarone infusion.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn view of uncontrolled sugars and ketoacidosis patient was started on insulin infusion.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn view of hypotension - ? \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThere are various cardiovascular complications in ketoacidosis secondary to electrolyte disturbances and catecholamine release. Pulmonary edema can also result, and patients with acute myocardial infarction (MI) may be predisposed to ketoacidosis, which in turn further causes damage to the myocardium.11\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EKetoacidosis results in electrolyte imbalances, especially reductions in potassium, magnesium, and phosphorus, which can result in cardio-vascular complications if not carefully replaced\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.uspharmacist.com\/article\/cardiovascular-complications-of-ketoacidosis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnd in the end I would also like to emphasise on the importance of psychological factors in cardiovascular health. In this case the psychosocial factors of importance were that pt..son…whatever it is tell that .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC3653260\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: red;\"\u003EThe technical difficulties\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatients admitted with Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) are often volume depleted and require large volumes of intravenous fluids for resuscitation. Large volume resuscitation can have major impacts on the mortality, length of hospital stay in the Heart failure population with reduced ejection fraction. This is another issue in tackling this kind of patients.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EYou can mention about it but before that search and see if there are any guidelines to treat patients with DKAHF\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E------\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDKA valla oche electrolyte abnormalities (Mg,Po4,K) might have precipitated a PSVT,and PSVT could have triggered the heart failure.In that case the heart failure will recover after controlling the arrhythmia and electrolyte abn\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E------\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESo there are 4 possibilities\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.DKA causing heart failure due to acidosis causing myocardial depression\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.DKA,electrolyte abn,PSVT then heart failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.MI causing DKA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4.Plus or minus pre existing coronary artery disease that sometimes won’t be evident on echo.\u003C\/p\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"edit","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/3915536545816552289\/posts\/default\/4662768428935989374"},{"rel":"self","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/3915536545816552289\/posts\/default\/4662768428935989374"},{"rel":"alternate","type":"text/html","href":"https:\/\/ajayaddula.blogspot.com\/2024\/01\/60f-with-cad-heart-failure-with-reduced.html","title":"60\/F with CAD- heart failure with reduced ejection fraction on mechanical ventilator , severe lv dysfunction left upper lobe fungal ball aspergilloma , VT - This E log book also reflects my patient-centred online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\"I've been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of \"patient clinical data analysis\" to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings, investigations and come up with a diagnosis and treatment plan\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E50 year old male daily wage labourer\u0026nbsp; presented to the casualty with the complains of\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERight lower limb ulcers and swelling since 1 month\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eshortness of breath since 10 days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Epatient was apparently asymptomatic 1 month ago he then had an thorn prick injury to his right leg , following the injury 2nd day patient had mild redness and swelling over that region, the swelling progressed gradually and started developing ulcers over that region, there was blacking discoloration over that region and gradual pus discharge from that site , the wound gradually extended to the right foot and leg .\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHistory of fever following swelling of the right lower limb , high grade , associated with chills and rigors intermittent , no diurnal variation and relieved after medication, fever subsided after 5 days.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient was taken to near by hospital and was diagnosed to have right lower limb cellulitis with acute kidney injury (AKI )\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ewhere debridement was done and left femoral catheter was placed , during the hospital stay patient received 7 sessions of haemodialysis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient started experiencing shortness of breath since 10 days insidious in onset and gradually progressive progressed from grade II to IV associated with orthopnea and no PND\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo diurnal variation and no seasonal variation of shortness of breath\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo history of\u0026nbsp; cough , chest pain , pedal edema,\u0026nbsp; vomitings, giddiness, palpitations\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERoutine 2d echo done there showed RWMA and EF of 35% and patient was referred to our hospital for further evaluation and management\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Ch1 style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003ETime line of events\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/h1\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient is the 4 th born member of the family 3 elder sisters and 2 younger sisters and brothers\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient is illiterate and helped their parents in farming\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EGot married at the age of 19 years to 15 year old women and non consanguinous type of marriage\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHad 2 childern one male and female\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient daily routine is to get up at 5 am go to farm for milking the cows and feeding them , comes back home at 7 am, has breakfast at 9 am and goes to daily wage labourer work - where he used to carry mud and\u0026nbsp; other agricultural goods and goes for ploughing comes back home at 6 pm then goes out with his friends for recreational activity consumed daily 2 quarters of alcohol and 12-16 beedis for day and goes to bed at 9 pm after having dinner\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient was doing well till the last 10 years\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E10 years ago his son who was normal and healthy all of the sudden\u0026nbsp; was found dead at home by the evening they came home from the work\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFrom then patient was more addicted to alcohol and smoking and never used to have proper food and used to feel saying that my son was dead\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHis daughter got married 6 years ago\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFrom then the patient and his wife were living together and doing their daily work and patient continued to drink alcohol in increasing quantity and consumed 20 beedi per day\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2 years ago in the month of February patient had sudden onset chest pain, giddiness\u0026nbsp; and shortness of breath\u0026nbsp; and was diagnosed to have acute MI and angiogram was done PTCA was done patient was discharged with rosuvastatin20 mg + ecosprin 75 mg + clopidogrel 75 mg , carvedilol 3.125 mg.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient was using regular medication for his heart problem since then\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESix months later he was diagnosed to have hypertension and was started on medication\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2 months later he was diagnosed with hypothyroidism and was started on thyronorm 25mcg\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient was using all these medications and was doing well and since his heart surgery he was restricted to home and did not go for workk\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1 month ago he developed thorn prick injury and eventually AKI and heart failure and 7 sessions of HD and wound debridement was done and was referred to our hospital\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Ch1 style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003EPast history\u003C\/h1\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EH\/O\u0026nbsp;
